title: Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Banking: Evidence from Bibliometric Analysis of Collaborative Networks and Research Trends
affiliations: Green University of Bangladesh

detail.title: Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Banking: Evidence from Bibliometric Analysis of Collaborative Networks and Research Trends
detail.abstract: In this study, we examine the research trends and collaboration networks in AI-driven transformation in banking by utilizing 751 Scopus-indexed documents from 2020 to 2026. We found that the number of publications continues to grow until 2024, and the literature is spread out over a series of conference proceedings, with a core set of highly cited foundational papers that define the overall landscape of research. In addition, keyword analysis and mapping of conceptual structure indicate a core set of research focused on applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning to risk management, fraud detection, cybersecurity, and market analysis. Thematic mapping of the search results shows that "artificial intelligence in banking" is a core theme, while generative AI, including ChatGPT and large language models, is a niche theme. The motor themes quadrant shows a sparse set of papers, which indicates that cutting-edge areas are still in their infancy. Further, we found that national production is dominated by a single predominant producer, while fragmented co-authorship networks are evident, with a mere 23.7% international collaboration. The study further proposes a future research agenda that includes the integration of GenAI with fundamental banking tasks, adversarial robustness, explainability and fairness, and impact, with the aim of shifting from a niche theme to a field-defining motor theme. This broadening area of artificial intelligence in banking also accelerates SDG 8(Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 9(Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure).

title: The Influence of Mobile Payment App Characteristics on Impulse Buying: The Mediating Role of Utilitarian and Hedonic Value
affiliations: Islamic University of Science and Technology, Islamic University of Science and Technology, Islamic University of Science and Technology and Islamic University of Science and Technology

detail.title: The Influence of Mobile Payment App Characteristics on Impulse Buying: The Mediating Role of Utilitarian and Hedonic Value
detail.abstract: Purpose: The rapid growth of Mobile Payment Applications (MPAs) has reshaped consumer purchasing behavior by integrating payment convenience with engaging digital experiences. Despite the growing popularity of these applications, limited research has explored how specific mobile payment app characteristics contribute to impulse buying. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework (S-O-R), this study examines the influence of mobile payment app characteristics on impulse buying through the mediating roles of utilitarian and hedonic value.Design/Methodology/Approach: A single cross-sectional survey design was used to collect 426 valid responses from MPA users in India, using a purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) in Smart PLS 4.0. The study integrates the S-O-R framework with the Mobile Technology Acceptance Model (MTAM) to examine how mobile ease of use, mobile usefulness, perceived interactivity, visual appeal, and promotional programs shape Generation Y and Generation Z consumers’ utilitarian and hedonic value derived from using MPAs, and whether these value perceptions, in turn, drive impulse buying.Findings: The findings of the study reveal that Mobile Ease of Use, Promotional Programs, and Visual Appeal significantly influence Utilitarian Value, while Perceived Interactivity, Promotional Programs, and Visual Appeal significantly influence Hedonic Value. Mobile Usefulness showed no significant effect on either value dimension.  The study also confirmed the significant and direct impact of Utilitarian and Hedonic Value on Impulse Buying, with Hedonic Value emerging as the stronger predictor. Additionally, mediation analysis revealed that Utilitarian Value mediated the relationship between Promotional Programs and Impulse Buying, while Hedonic Value mediated the relationships between Perceived Interactivity, Promotional Programs, and Visual Appeal with Impulse Buying.Practical Implications: This study offers valuable insights for mobile payment service providers, marketers, and policymakers by demonstrating how specific app characteristics influence Impulse Buying through Utilitarian and Hedonic Value. The findings suggest that Visual Appeal, Interactivity, and Promotional Programs are stronger levers for building value perceptions than functional usefulness alone, and can inform how marketers structure promotional campaigns, how providers prioritize design investment, and how policymakers approach responsible digital payment practices that strike a balance  between business objectives and consumer welfare.Originality/Value: Previous literature on MPAs has largely focused on antecedents of adoption and usage, with relatively little attention paid to how the use of MPAs inadvertently affects purchase decisions. By making payment fast, seamless, and enjoyable, MPAs may encourage consumers to follow through on impulsive urges more easily than traditional payment methods. As payments form a critical part of daily consumption process, exploring the downstream impact of emerging mobile payment technologies on consumers’ purchase behaviour and the underlying psychological mechanisms can provide new insights for individuals and societies to manage consumption activities. title: Views on Professional Leadership in public professions today; an exploration into professional leadership
affiliations: NHL Stenden University of Applied Sciences, Fontys University of Applied Sciences and NHL Stenden University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Views on Professional Leadership in public professions today; an exploration into professional leadership
detail.abstract: Professional Leadership is an upcoming phenomenon and competence in public professions that suggests that professionals themselves take the lead in performing quality societal services. Up till today, professional leadership is often studied and described in contexts of a specific profession or public domain such as healthcare or education. Three such studies of the authors, on nursing leadership, teacher leadership and self-leadership of healthcare workers, were used to develop an enriched definition of professional leadership applicable for (public) professions in general. Starting out with presentations of their work and explorative dialogues, steps from concept development theories were used later to analyse and define (clusters of) similar characteristics of professional leadership found in all three studies. The findings of this exploration show seven defining clusters of characteristics: autonomy, assertiveness, moral values and commitment, expertise, reflection, cooperation and social support, and individual qualities. Most of these characteristics can also be seen as conditional and/or consequential and/or contextual factors. There is overlap of professional leadership with professionalism as a concept. However, self-influencing strategies and assertiveness related characteristics seem to differentiate the concepts from one another. Professional identity and identity forming within a specific profession and societal context in general, are also to be seen as closely related to (developing) professional leadership. In conclusion, professional leadership is a multifactorial competence in which seven clusters of characteristics need to be developed and employed in an integrated way.

title: The Operator-Built System: Capability, Builder's Flood, and the Return to Knowledge Management
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Operator-Built System: Capability, Builder's Flood, and the Return to Knowledge Management

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author developed the systems and the curation architecture described here for his own use across professional, academic and personal work . No external funding supported this work. No commercial interest is asserted.

detail.abstract:
That a domain expert can direct artificial intelligence to build and operate working systems is established, and is this paper’s starting condition rather than its finding. What is less examined is what operating such systems obliges of the person accountable for them.
In an operator-built system no reviewer stands between output and use, so every output requires the operator's judgement — and that judgement cannot be returned to the AI. Several models independently reviewed a routine failing in production and each reported it correct, because the fault lay in the specification the code faithfully implemented. A structured multi-role review reached unanimous agreement because none of its reviewers had received instructions.
If judgement is required per output and outputs arrive continuously, adjudication capacity becomes binding. This paper names that condition builder's flood. The case is a personal knowledge management system spanning professional, academic and personal domains, each with a distinct standard of correctness and none able to pass the burden anywhere. The SECI lineage and its generative-AI extensions model knowledge conversion without a parameter for the converter's capacity — an omission that was harmless while generation ran at human pace. The response is curation, its rules established by failure rather than principle. Curation is knowledge management, and the constraint has moved from capture to gating.

title: Prompt Engineering as an Expression Game: A Dramaturgical Theory of Human-AI Interaction
affiliations: , RMIT University, Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University), Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University) and Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University)

detail.title: Prompt Engineering as an Expression Game: A Dramaturgical Theory of Human-AI Interaction

declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subject was involved in the study.

detail.abstract: Prompt engineering has been posited as a new skill following the widespread availability of generative AI and tools powered by large language models. Efforts to strengthen human capabilities in crafting effective prompts, alongside evaluations of the efficacy of generative AI tools in producing quality responses, have become focal points for researchers, developers, and users. As a result, prompt engineering is often viewed merely as a process of textual formulation. In response, this article argues that prompt engineering is an expressive game between human prompters and generative AI tools. It shows the human prompter's capacity to observe and engage with the AI tool's ability to discern tasks embedded within the prompt. Thus, prompt engineering is not only an art of composing commands through language; it also reflects the capacities of both the human prompter and the AI tool to perform distinct roles as they respond to one another concurrently.

title: Event-Based Phase modelling and Forecasting with Time-Variant Fuzzy Time Series: An Application to Electricity Consumption
affiliations: Government Victoria College, Arizona State University (ASU) - National Institute of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Event-Based Phase modelling and Forecasting with Time-Variant Fuzzy Time Series: An Application to Electricity Consumption
detail.abstract: Non-stationary time series frequently exhibit structural variations due to changes in system conditions and the influence of external factors, making accurate forecasting a challenging task. These variations may arise from uncontrollable events such as pandemics and natural disruptions, or from controllable interventions such as policy regulations, operational changes, and economic decisions. Such external influences can significantly alter the behaviour of the study variable and thereby induce distinct temporal phases in the time series. Conventional statistical models and fuzzy time series approaches often rely on a single global structure, which may be inadequate when the underlying data behaviour changes across different phases. Although the phase-cum-time variant fuzzy time series (PTVFTS) framework accommodates phase-wise variations in non-stationary time series, meaningful identification of phases based on externally induced behavioural changes can further improve its applicability to real-world systems. Motivated by this perspective, the present study applies an externally driven phase modelling strategy within the PTVFTS framework for forecasting electricity consumption under different COVID-related phases.

title: Dynamic Decision-Making Structures in Social Dilemmas: Attachment Style and Three-Step Markov Chain Network Analysis of the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma

detail.abstract: Why do some people sustain cooperation in repeated exchange while others become trapped in mutual defection? Answering this requires treating cooperation as a decision process—a sequence of transitions between behavioral states—rather than a summary rate. We examined whether a stable psychological individual difference, adult attachment, predicts the dynamics of cooperative and exploitative decision-making. 171 adults played the iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma against five opponents. Among psychopathy, bullying experience, and attachment, only the anxiety-by-avoidance interaction predicted a general exploitation–cooperation tendency (b = .187, p = .012), identifying attachment as the operative individual difference. We then classified participants as secure, mixed, or fearful and modeled their choices as three-step Markov transition networks, testing group differences with bootstrap and permutation methods. The groups were distinguished by decision structure, not by how much they cooperated. Secure participants uniquely preserved a recovery path from mutual defection to cooperation when facing a reciprocal opponent; fearful participants could not stabilize the defensive alternation needed against a relentless defector; mixed participants failed to maintain extended mutual cooperation sequences even against an unconditional cooperator. These results locate attachment in the psychological machinery of economic decision-making: as a stable individual difference, it predicts the resilience and path-dependence of cooperative decisions—which interaction regimes people fall into, and who can leave a non-cooperative regime—an account that aggregate cooperation rates leave invisible.

title: The Bare-Backbone Workflow (BBW): A Framework Methodology for Translating Strategy into Execution
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Bare-Backbone Workflow (BBW): A Framework Methodology for Translating Strategy into Execution

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Zenodo Working Paper Repository, published 31 May 2026. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20475083

detail.abstract:
The Bare-Backbone Workflow (BBW) is a practitioner-built framework methodology designed to address the tension gap between post-decision strategic execution and executives’ interpretations to bridge the operational execution. Developed through professional practice and reshaped with academic knowledge and research, across the pharmaceutical industry and subsequently applied across multiple domains including trading, ERP restructuring, manufacturing operations, and systems designs, automation and/or integration, the BBW provides a disciplined approach to translating strategic decisions and connecting them to technical and operational foundations before and throughout the execution.

The methodology operates across three dimensions: the Bare Backbone, which defines the irreducible minimum of operational stages; the Integration-Architecture Layer, which establishes connectivity, dependencies, interdependencies, data generation points, and approval gates between those essential stages; and the Elaboration Layer, which accommodates unlimited domain-specific extension built or future strategic shift on top of that foundation. The first two dimensions are fixed and transferable across different domains. The third is variable and defined by the application and organisational strategic vision. 

This working paper presents the methodology: its conceptual foundation, three-dimension architecture, implementation logic, transferability across domains, and the common failure patterns observed through professional practice. The BBW is positioned as a complementary bridge to existing strategy frameworks, project management methodologies, and process improvement tools, occupying the space, as an interface, between strategic intent and operational execution that other disciplines have only partially addressed.

title: How Important are Context-Specific Factors Work-Home Interference for Turnover and Turnover Intentions in Health Care Occupations: A Prospective Study
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How Important are Context-Specific Factors Work-Home Interference for Turnover and Turnover Intentions in Health Care Occupations: A Prospective Study
detail.abstract: Background: Maintaining a stable healthcare workforce is a major challenge for healthcare systems worldwide. Employee turnover can disrupt continuity of care, increase organizational costs, and potentially affect patient safety. Previous research indicates that work environment factors and work-home interference are associated with turnover intentions, yet the role of context-specific predictors in actual turnover among healthcare workers remains understudied. Whether turnover intention is a sufficient proxy for actual turnover also remains unclear.Objective: This study examines (i) whether emotional demands, illegitimate tasks, and dissatisfaction with workplace service quality predict actual turnover and turnover intention; (ii) if similar patterns exist for both outcomes; (iii) the role of work-home interference in these associations; and (iv) whether turnover intention contributes to the prediction of actual turnover.Setting(s): The study sample was drawn from the Swedish Longitudinal Occupational Survey of Health (SLOSH) 2022-2025, a nationwide survey with repeated questionnaire assessments.Participants: Analyses were restricted to participants who worked 30% or more in a health care profession, were 66 years or younger at baseline and responded at baseline and to at least one of the following waves (N=982). Methods: Hierarchical logistic regression analyses were conducted to examine prospective associations between work environment characteristics, work-home interference, and subsequent actual turnover and turnover intention.Results: In unadjusted bivariate models, all work environment factors showed statistically significant associations with both outcomes (e.g. for actual turnover: emotional demands OR=1.37 (95% CI: 1.05-1.81), unreasonable tasks OR=1.49 (95% CI: 1.13-1.85). After adjustment for work-home interference, none of the work environment characteristics were associated with actual turnover. For turnover intentions, the associations remained statistically significant after adjusting for work-home interference, except for emotional demands (e.g., unreasonable tasks OR=1.57 (95% CI: 1.14-2.16; dissatisfaction with service quality OR=1.52 (95% CI: 1.14-2.02). Turnover intention was associated with increased odds for subsequent actual turnover after accounting for work environment and work-home interference (e.g., controlling for age, occupational group, emotional demands and work-home interference OR=3.02; 95% CI: 1.76-5.19)Conclusions: The study extends previous turnover research by examining both turnover intention and actual turnover in relation to healthcare-specific work environment characteristics. We find that context specific work environment factors contribute beyond general work demands to turnover intention. While work environment predicted intention to leave, actual turnover seems to manifest first when work interferes with private life. In addition to work-home interference, turnover intention also contributed to later actual turnover.

title: Behavior-Aware Traffic Prediction for Hurricane Evacuations via an AIRL-Inspired Adversarial Behavior-Learning Framework
affiliations: Florida State University, Florida State University, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering, Florida State University, , Nanjing University of Science and Technology and Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University

detail.title: Behavior-Aware Traffic Prediction for Hurricane Evacuations via an AIRL-Inspired Adversarial Behavior-Learning Framework
detail.abstract: Accurate traffic prediction during hurricane evacuations is essential for effective emergency management, yet conventional approaches may not fully capture the behavioral dynamics underlying evacuation traffic. This study develops a behavior-aware framework that combines an adversarial behavior-learning component inspired by Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning (AIRL) with deep learning models. Using probe vehicle trajectories, the behavior-learning component identifies route-choice patterns and produces two model-internal behavioral features: route-choice entropy and maximum transition probability. These features are incorporated into LSTM models for short-term speed prediction and MLP models for long-term congestion classification, with strict temporal separation between predictors and targets. The framework is evaluated using probe vehicle data from Hurricane Sally in Escambia County, Florida, an evacuation event shaped by pandemic-era non-congregate sheltering guidance. AIRL-inspired features improve short-term speed prediction across all four forecast horizons, reducing MAE by 0.5–0.85 kph, and improve long-term congestion classification, increasing macro-F1 by approximately 0.05. Although baseline accuracy is high (96–98\%), macro-F1 provides a more informative measure under class imbalance. Improvements remain statistically significant after Holm–Bonferroni correction, with effect sizes considered alongside p-values given serial correlation in the observations. Transfer learning from normal traffic provides, at most, a marginal and non-significant benefit at 15 minutes and no consistent improvement at longer horizons. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of incorporating learned route-choice information into evacuation traffic prediction while motivating further causal and survey-based research to establish the behavioral meaning of these learned features.

title: Reads over Atom Spaces: A Mathematical View of Context, Retrieval, and Parameter Routing in Language Models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Reads over Atom Spaces: A Mathematical View of Context, Retrieval, and Parameter Routing in Language Models
detail.abstract: Attention, external retrieval, and parameter-expert routing all compute query-conditioned weighted reads. We provide a common analytical lens based on valued atom spaces $(\Om,\mathcal F,\nu,v)$ and the read operator $R(x;\Om)=\int_\Om v(\omega)\,d\mu_x(\omega)$, which reduces to a softmax-weighted value combination under a counting measure. First, we derive a Lipschitz-margin sufficient condition for an inserted record to enter top-$k$ retrieval. On 384-dimensional semantic embeddings, the condition is vacuous even when insertion succeeds. Second, we derive exact softmax-tail certificates and an error-budgeted truncation rule. On synthetic corpora with $N=25{,}000$, the certificate selects 52--86\% of atoms, confirming that it certifies approximation error but is not a sublinear retrieval method. Third, signed reference measures permit exact cancellation of a matched external record by an anti-atom; a 3,000-trial stress test shows that this cancellation is highly sensitive to key perturbations. On CounterFact-500, held-out ROC calibration of a frozen-MiniLM activation threshold ($\theta^*=0.55$; test AUC $0.829$) increases paraphrase activation from 38.2\% to 53.2\%, while neighborhood false activation rises from 9.6\% to 16.1\%. Matched-scale GPT-2 experiments place this gated retrieval beside a rank-one parametric reference and GRACE, revealing a generalization--locality trade-off associated with their key spaces. Controlled routing and first-token steering experiments are reported as diagnostics, with their limitations stated explicitly. We do not propose a new editing method or claim superiority; rather, we offer a shared vocabulary and empirical calibrations of what retrieval, metric, and tail arguments can certify.

title: The safety of leachate-irrigated Medicago sativa: A Sub-Chronic toxicological study on Wistar Rats
affiliations: Hassan II University, Hassan II University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Mohammed VI University of Health Sciences, Ibn Rochd University Hospital Center, Ibn Rochd University Hospital Center, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Chouaib Doukkali University and Hassan II University

detail.title: The safety of leachate-irrigated Medicago sativa: A Sub-Chronic toxicological study on Wistar Rats
detail.abstract: The potential of diluted landfill leachate as a source of nutrients for crops in semi-arid regions of Morocco is the focus of this research. In previous work, we established 7% (v·v⁻¹) as the optimal concentration for irrigating Medicago sativa. In the current study, plants grown with irrigation at this previously optimised 7% concentration demonstrated healthy and vigorous growth, with no signs of stress. To assess the safety of this agricultural approach, the leachate was administered to Wistar rats for 28 days. The rats maintained normal behaviour and experienced consistent weight gain. In addition, there were no differences in relative liver or kidney weights when compared to control animals. Increased alanine aminotransferase (ALAT) activity was observed in leachate-treated male rats (106.9 U.L⁻¹), as well as increased creatinine levels (1.61 mg.L⁻¹). In contrast, treated female rats had decreased ALAT (88.3 U.L⁻¹) and increased creatinine (1.71 mg.L⁻¹) levels. Decreased alkaline phosphatase activity and increased urea levels were found for both sexes. Histologically, the livers and kidneys from the treated rats retained their normal architecture, and no evidence of inflammation, necrosis, or degeneration was noted. The biochemical changes observed in the treated rats were not indicative of structural toxicity. Thus, this study provides preliminary evidence to support the agricultural use of landfill leachate at the optimised concentration, but identifies the need for longer-term toxicity testing to better elucidate safe exposure levels.

title: Where Platforms Win: Local Competitive Advantage in Location-Bound Platforms and Its Aggregation into Firm-Level Rents
affiliations: , Ritsumeikan University, Institute of Science Tokyo and

detail.title: Where Platforms Win: Local Competitive Advantage in Location-Bound Platforms and Its Aggregation into Firm-Level Rents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI [grant number JP23K01561].

detail.abstract: Platform competition has long been expected to converge on a single winner. Yet platforms whose transactions are fulfilled through physical movement and completed within a local market-food delivery, ride-hailing, and spot-work matching, which we call location-bound platforms-depart from this prediction: independent platforms persist alongside the leaders, market leadership changes hands, and within-city duopolies endure. More fundamentally, the same firm's competitive position differs across local markets. This integrative review asks why competitive advantage in location-bound platforms differs across local markets, and under what conditions local advantage aggregates into firm-level rents and persists. Bridging management research, which has the firm's perspective but lacks spatial mechanisms, and economics, which has the spatial mechanisms but lacks the perspective of competitive advantage, we lower the unit of analysis from the firm to the local market and organize the mechanisms into three layers: spatial market structure, the appropriability structure of competitive resources, and competitive dynamics. Their integration yields two baseline propositions and six propositions. The central proposition is that local advantage aggregates into firm-level rents to the degree that local resources are inimitable by rivals and the routines that form them are replicable within the firm across local markets-combining the inter-firm question of the resource-based view with the intra-firm question of replication research, which prior work has not linked. Even aggregated advantage can be eroded under user multihoming through continued defensive expenditure and the decoupling of market position from profitability. We close with a research agenda and identify the Japanese market as a setting for discriminating competing predictions.

title: Electricity tariff design, private investment in PV and batteries, and the distribution of impacts of tariff change
affiliations: ZHAW Zurich University of Applied Sciences and ZHAW School of Management and Law

detail.title: Electricity tariff design, private investment in PV and batteries, and the distribution of impacts of tariff change
detail.abstract: We study the distribution of impacts across households when dynamic electricity tariffs are introduced as a means to promote system friendly behavior of consumers (households) in Switzerland. For this we combine a building level model of rational investments in solar photovoltaics and batteries with household data for analyzing distributional effects across households. We find that the transition to dynamic tariffs somewhat favours high income households in the short term but is rather distributionally neutral in the long term when heat-pumps and battery electric vehicles (BEVs) are more widely spread. In the short term, retirees are the group that is least able to profit from dynamic tariffs; in the long term, home owners can better profit from dynamic tariffs than tenants. However, heterogeneity of impacts between households within each household group is considerable. For long term results, we can show that our results are crucially dependent on assumptions about electricity price levels and patterns.

title: Evaluating Learned Accelerometer Representations Beyond a Transported PREDICT Score for Cardiovascular Risk
affiliations: Auckland University of Technology, Auckland University of Technology, Auckland University of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Evaluating Learned Accelerometer Representations Beyond a Transported PREDICT Score for Cardiovascular Risk
detail.abstract: Background: Clinical cardiovascular risk scores do not directly measure habitual movement. We tested whether average-day accelerometer representations add risk information beyond a transported PREDICT score and transparent activity summaries.Methods: We analysed 4,341 adults aged 30–79 years from the 2003–2006 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, including 192 fatal heart-or-cerebrovascular events. Wear-aware averaging yielded one 1,440-minute profile per participant. Frozen PREDICT-BMI coeﬀicients supplied the clinical prior, and each representation learned an additive ridge-Cox correction. Comparators captured overall activity, active minutes and daily rhythm. Principal-component, reconstruction-autoencoder, masked-autoencoder, contrastive and outcome-aware representations were evaluated on common folds. Five outer and three inner folds separated model selection from evaluation. The primary contrast tested a nested-selected autoencoder beyond daily-rhythm features; fixed eight-dimensional comparisons were exploratory.Results: Transported PREDICT achieved a C-index of 0.8424 (95% confidence interval 0.8138–0.8681). The primary augmented model achieved 0.8452, but its paired improvement over daily rhythm was uncertain (0.00287,95% confidence interval -0.00281 to 0.00903). Across five outer fold partitions, the mean improvement was 0.00094. Exploratory contrastive learning produced the strongest point estimate (C-index 0.8464) and improved by 0.00198 (0.00010–0.00375) over the fixed daily-rhythm comparator. Prediction-error and decision-utility improvements were inconsistent.Conclusions: Average-day accelerometry contained a small additional ranking signal, and contrastive learning was the most promising exploratory objective. Improved absolute-risk accuracy and clinical utility were not es- tablished. Independent endpoint-aligned validation is required before clinical use.

title: From Transition Hedge to Energy Risk Factor: Dynamic Carbon–Energy Dependence Across Market Regimes
affiliations: and University of Piraeus

detail.title: From Transition Hedge to Energy Risk Factor: Dynamic Carbon–Energy Dependence Across Market Regimes
detail.abstract: Although previous studies document time-varying carbon-energy dependence, it remains unclear when the relation between European Union Allowance (EUA) prices and brown-equity returns changes sign, how much of that dependence reflects common energy shocks, and whether dynamic carbon hedges retain value outside the estimation window. Using 3,339 synchronized daily observations over 2013-2026 on EUA futures, European and US oil-and-gas equity, clean-energy equity, Brent crude, and a nested Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF) natural-gas sample, we combine endogenous structural-break tests, factor-adjusted dynamic conditional correlation (DCC) and asymmetric DCC (ADCC) models, tail-dependence methods, and dynamic hedging. Bai-Perron tests identify stable breaks around March 2020 and September 2021; BIC also selects a terminal break whose exact date is sensitive to trimming. Conditioning on Brent attenuates the EUA loading by 64% for European brown equity and 55% for US brown equity; adding TTF renders the European loading statistically insignificant. Factor-adjusted ADCC correlations fall by about 75%, and by roughly 90% for the European pair in the TTF sample. Downside dependence is strongest for US energy equity. In a recursive pseudo-out-of-sample exercise, dynamic hedging outperforms a static benchmark on average, but gains concentrate in 2020-2021 and vanish in the baseline terminal regime. Carbon is therefore neither an unconditional transition hedge nor an unconditional risk factor: its relation to brown equity is state-dependent and largely associated with observable energy shocks. The results support modeling carbon-equity dependence jointly with oil and gas and evaluating hedge value regime by regime.

title: The Greening Effect of Green Bonds on Corporate Energy Transition: Micro Evidence from Chinese A-Listed Firms aLI Bohua1, aSUI Yuan2, aJIA Kaiwei3, aWU Jinjin4
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Liaoning Technical University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Greening Effect of Green Bonds on Corporate Energy Transition: Micro Evidence from Chinese A-Listed Firms aLI Bohua1, aSUI Yuan2, aJIA Kaiwei3, aWU Jinjin4
detail.abstract: Amidst deepening global climate governance, whether green bonds genuinely drive corporate energy restructuring remains contested. This study examines the causal effect of green bond issuance on corporate energy structure transition using a unique micro-dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2024. Grounded in a Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) production function framework, we model green bonds as a mechanism that reduces the user cost of clean energy capital, thereby altering firms' optimal fossil-to-clean energy substitution path. To establish causality, we employ two-way fixed effects and an ensemble Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DML) estimator, which flexibly captures treatment effect heterogeneity while addressing high-dimensional confounding. Empirical results reveal three novel findings: First, green bond issuance induces a significantly positive and scale-increasing substitution effect​ toward cleaner energy. Second, green technology innovation​ mediates this transition, with incremental innovation​ demonstrating a stronger transmission channel than radical innovation—suggesting that green finance primarily facilitates gradual optimization rather than disruptive technological leaps. Third, and counter-intuitively, financing constraints positively moderate​ the greening effect, whereas high ESG ratings exhibit negative moderation, revealing a "diminishing marginal return" pattern for sustainability incumbents. These findings provide micro-empirical evidence for calibrating green finance policies and highlight that green bonds are most potent for firms facing urgent transition pressures.

title: CrossHallu: Do Hallucination Signals Generalize Across Languages and Domains in Large Language Models' Internals?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Imam Abdulrahman Bin Faisal University and King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals (KFUPM)

detail.title: CrossHallu: Do Hallucination Signals Generalize Across Languages and Domains in Large Language Models' Internals?
detail.abstract: Recent hallucination detection techniques in large language models (LLMs) focus on directly extracting features from a model's internal representations and training a classifier on these features to detect hallucinations, demonstrating promising results. Notwithstanding this advancement, most internal-state hallucination detection techniques have been explored predominantly in English, raising the question of whether such internal signals generalize across different languages and domains. To address this gap, we present CrossHallu, the first study to evaluate the cross-lingual and cross-domain generalization of hallucination detection using internal representations from six LLMs on the generative question-answering task. We conduct a systematic evaluation between Arabic and English using TruthfulQA, its Arabic-translated version, and HalluScore. This evaluation encompasses monolingual training and testing, cross-lingual transfer, cross-domain transfer, and combined cross-lingual and cross-domain transfer. The results reveal that internal-state hallucination signals in LLMs transfer across languages and domains for most models, with cross-lingual performance highly dependent on both class separability and language alignment in the feature space, whereas cross-domain transfer within Arabic varies depending on the training and testing datasets used for the hallucination detector. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/aishaalansari57/CrossHal.

title: Price Formation and Value Factors in the Nordic Day-Ahead Market: A Methodological Synthesis of Bidding Behavior and Wind Penetration
affiliations: University of Bergen, University of Bergen, University of Bergen and NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Business and Management Science

detail.title: Price Formation and Value Factors in the Nordic Day-Ahead Market: A Methodological Synthesis of Bidding Behavior and Wind Penetration
detail.abstract: The ongoing transition toward variable renewable energy (VRE) in the Nordic electricity market challenges traditional models of price formation. Optimization-based long-run planning tools frequently underestimate short-term price volatility because they abstract away the discrete, stepwise nature of empirical supply and demand curves. This paper synthesizes three recent methodological developments to better capture these dynamics: (1) a simplified, deterministic representation of the Euphemia algorithm to isolate bidding behavior; (2) a bin-based regression methodology to empirically map VRE capacity additions onto the discrete steps of the supply curve; and (3) an optimization routine for the displacement and reinjection of reservoir-based hydropower bids in response to wind-induced merit-order effects. Applying this combined framework to a 2050 scenario for the Norwegian market reveals that increased wind penetration maintains median prices but significantly amplifies price risk during a minority of high-value scarcity hours. We demonstrate that the value factor of wind power exhibits a threshold relationship with market strain, and that treating the electricity price as a discrete staircase is essential for producing realistic estimates of market volatility and asset valuation in hydro-dominated systems.

title: Passive investors, active moves: ETF participation in IPOs​
affiliations: University of Melbourne - Department of Finance, Xiamen University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Hainan University

detail.title: Passive investors, active moves: ETF participation in IPOs​
detail.abstract: We examine the pervasive participation of index ETFs in IPOs in the Chinese stock market, where ETFs exploit underpricing to generate returns of approximately 4.56% per annum. However, this discretionary activity also increases non-fundamental volatility and short-term return reversals among constituent stocks, constituting a pecuniary externality. Exploiting a policy shock as a quasi-natural experiment, we construct an instrumental variable to establish causality for both the private benefits and market-wide costs. Our findings highlight the dual nature of index ETF activeness: discretionary strategies can enhance investor returns while imposing costs on the broader market.

title: A Comparative Analysis of SME Development Models: Lessons for Bangladesh from South Korea
affiliations: University of Chittagong

detail.title: A Comparative Analysis of SME Development Models: Lessons for Bangladesh from South Korea

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None to declare.no conflicts of interest

detail.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) serve as the structural backbone of economic growth, employment generation, and industrial innovation in developing and developed nations alike. This paper conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis between the highly successful SME development model of South Korea-which underpinned the "Miracle on the Han River"-and the rapidly evolving but structurally constrained SME sector of Bangladesh. While Bangladesh's SMEs contribute significantly to labor employment, they face severe challenges in technology adoption, institutional financing, and global supply chain integration. Conversely, South Korea's transition into a high-tech export economy was driven by integrating SMEs into industrial networks supported by robust credit guarantees and state-led technological incubation. By analyzing the institutional framework of South Korea, this study provides actionable policy recommendations for Bangladesh to leverage SME expansion as a critical strategy for sustainable economic development post-LDC graduation.

title: The Congregation Economy: An African Theory of Opportunity, Coordination, and Growth

detail.title: The Congregation Economy: An African Theory of Opportunity, Coordination, and Growth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of Interest. i Am an independent researcher presenting original theoretical work.
declarations.funderStatement: No body or institution(s) funded the research.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Congregation Economy-a theoretical framework proposing that wealth creation begins with human congregation, not capital. The central proposition: congregation is the necessary condition for opportunity, and coordination is the necessary condition for value creation. Through a sequence of congregation, need, friction, and coordination, the paper derives six formal laws governing how economic opportunity emerges, is captured, and compounds into sustained wealth. The paper extends the foundational Human Congregation Theory to encompass three tiers of congregation-Physical, Practice, and Condition-addressing the limitation of spatial-only congregation models. The framework is grounded primarily in African economic contexts, including Nigerian motor parks, urban markets, and the M-Pesa ecosystem, arguing that Africa's most significant development opportunities are already latent within its existing congregation density. The paper positions the Congregation Economy as an earlier-stage theory of opportunity formation relative to established frameworks including Smith, Porter, and Christensen.

title: Fiduciary Futures: Rethinking Pensions as Engines of Sustainable Development in Africa

detail.title: Fiduciary Futures: Rethinking Pensions as Engines of Sustainable Development in Africa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I am a development economist and financial sector practitioner with over 15 years of senior leadership experience across Ghana's pension, asset management, and wealth management industries. This includes prior employment at Old Mutual Pension Trust, UMB-Investment Holdings Limited, EDC Investments Limited, First Atlantic Asset Management Ltd, and Databank Asset Management Services Ltd. I am currently a Non-Resident Fellow at the Center for Policy Scrutiny (CPS) Ghana and previously held a fellowship at the International Growth Centre (IGC) Ghana. This research was conducted independently and does not represent the views of any of these organizations. My professional experience directly informs the research questions and policy recommendations presented in this study, particularly regarding pension fund governance, regulatory constraints, and the structural barriers to productive capital deployment in Ghana and across Africa. I declare no other competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by the International Growth Centre (IGC) through a competitive fellowship awarded to me as part of its programme to build local research capacity for evidence-based policymaking in Ghana. The IGC provided financial support for my research activities, including data collection, analysis, and dissemination of findings. The views expressed in this paper are my own and do not necessarily reflect those of the International Growth Centre or its partner institutions.

detail.abstract: This study asks whether Africa's rapidly growing pension fund assets are fulfilling their promised role as engines of economic growth. Using panel data from 54 African countries (1990–2024) and Bayesian linear regressions for Ghana, the analysis yields a consistent and robust null result: pension fund assets have no statistically significant effect on economic growth, either continent-wide or in Ghana. Panel evidence further reveals a negative association between pension fund growth and stock market capitalisation, suggesting that the overwhelming concentration of African pension portfolios in sovereign securities crowds out, rather than catalyses, financial market deepening. These findings are not a counsel of despair but a design opportunity. Ghana's regulatory framework already permits alternative investments and green bonds, yet no green bond has been issued. The study argues that by anchoring a national definition of "green" in Ghana's specific climate vulnerabilities, rising temperatures and coastal erosion, pension funds can be repositioned as anchor investors in a domestic green bond market. Policy recommendations target the NPRA, the Government of Ghana, and the Ghana Stock Exchange to transition pension capital from a passive holder of sovereign debt into a catalytic force for climate-aligned sustainable growth.

title: Thích Minh Tuệ as a Dhutaṅga Yogi: Religious Authority, Ascetic Practice, and Legitimacy Without Institutional Certification
affiliations: University of Illinois College of Medicine

detail.title: Thích Minh Tuệ as a Dhutaṅga Yogi: Religious Authority, Ascetic Practice, and Legitimacy Without Institutional Certification
detail.abstract:
Thích Minh Tuệ is a Vietnamese dhutaṅga (dhutanga) practitioner whose contested monastic status raises a broader question in Buddhist studies: how should religious authority grounded in observable ascetic practice be classified when institutional certification is absent or disputed? In May and June 2024 the Vietnam Buddhist Sangha declared that he is not a Buddhist monk, the Unified Buddhist Church of Vietnam measured his conduct against the Vinaya and concluded that he is, and the government’s Committee for Religious Affairs did not hold to a single position. This article argues that these rulings answer a question of practice in the vocabulary of jurisdiction, and it treats Vinaya ordination, membership in the Sangha, certification by it, state recognition and attainment as separate questions. Drawing on the author’s typology of existential witness, which explains how legitimacy can arise from publicly witnessed discipline, it proposes the yogi as a comparative category while keeping the Vietnamese term hành giả đầu đà primary. The classification is tested against the thirteen dhutaṅga observances of the Visuddhimagga, his conduct since 2018 as documented across several countries, and names conferred by observers who share no certifying body. His reported formation is read against Vietnamese monastic history: ordination long predates the Sangha, founded in 1981, whose documented rules on waiting periods, schooling and certificates date from 2013, so a two-year interval before higher ordination is compatible with the Vinaya and with Khất sĩ practice, although it cannot be independently verified. Objections are met from his refusal of titles, from the jurisdictional effect of relinquishing robe, honorific and affiliation, from Drikung Kagyu usage that places “Yogi” alongside khenpo and drupon, and from precedents in which authority did not depend on certification: Hòa thượng Nhẫn Tế, named Thubten Osall Lama by the Regent of Tibet in 1936, the lay Thiền master Tuệ Trung Thượng Sĩ, and, beyond Vietnam, figures such as Gyōki. The category makes no claim about attainment or ordination and confers no legal standing. Its value lies in allowing Buddhist asceticism to be described on the evidence while questions of ordination and institutional recognition remain open.

Keywords: Thích Minh Tuệ · Dhutaṅga · Dhutanga · yogi · Buddhist asceticism · religious authority · existential witness · Vinaya · monastic status · institutional legitimacy · Vietnam Buddhism · Vietnam Buddhist Sangha

title: Food–Energy-Water (FEW) Insecurity Nexus in Post-Crisis Sri Lanka
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Food–Energy-Water (FEW) Insecurity Nexus in Post-Crisis Sri Lanka
detail.abstract: This study examines the household-level food–energy–water (FEW) insecurity nexus in post-crisis Sri Lanka using BRIGHT survey data and a three-stage least-squares framework. Standardized indices were constructed for food, energy, and water insecurity, with the energy measure harmonized across two non-overlapping questionnaire forms. The final simultaneous-equation model was estimated for 1,456 households with complete data. Results confirm significant interdependence among the three insecurity dimensions. Energy insecurity increases food insecurity, while food insecurity exerts an even larger positive effect on energy insecurity. Food insecurity also significantly increases water insecurity, whereas the effect of water insecurity on food insecurity is positive but only marginally significant. Water insecurity is negatively associated with energy insecurity in the simultaneous system, while energy insecurity has no significant effect on water insecurity. Joint Wald tests reject the null of no nexus effects across the system. Education reduces food insecurity, household size increases energy insecurity, and water-collection time strongly increases water insecurity. Food-price and electricity-price shocks remain important post-crisis drivers. However, modest first-stage strength, rejection of overidentifying restrictions in the food equation, and complete-case sample reduction limit causal interpretation. The findings support integrated policies combining food assistance, energy affordability, reliable water access, and targeted social protection to strengthen household resilience in Sri Lanka.

title: Quantifying the costs and benefits of grid investments to decarbonize the European energy supply
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Groningen

detail.title: Quantifying the costs and benefits of grid investments to decarbonize the European energy supply
detail.abstract: Europe aims to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 through the electrification of fossil fuel-based energy demand and the large-scale deployment of renewable generation. Realizing these goals requires significant transmission expansion to facilitate cross-border electricity trade and to connect renewable generation sites to major demand centers. Additional transmission capacity entails high upfront costs and its future value depends on uncertain developments in generation technologies, fuel prices, and electricity demand. We examine how different grid investments perform under alternative future scenarios using a model-based case study on the decarbonization of the European energy supply. Quantifying the financial costs and benefits of three contrasting grid archetypes, we find that additional grid capacity comes at a sizable premium but offers substantial option value, specifically when nuclear generation becomes unavailable or relatively costly.

title: Systematic Risk Everywhere: Why Investors Overestimate Active Bets and Ignore the True Engine of Returns

detail.title: Systematic Risk Everywhere: Why Investors Overestimate Active Bets and Ignore the True Engine of Returns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No external funding was received for this research
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research

detail.abstract:
In modern portfolio construction, institutional and retail investors routinely employ multi-asset equity strategies that combine regional, sector-specific, thematic, and factor-tilted exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The underlying premise of these tactical overlays is that tilting exposure—such as overweighting tech megatrends, defense stocks, or style factors — generates non-market risk-adjusted excess returns (alpha) or structural diversification benefits. 

This paper critically re-examines this premise using a multi-factor empirical framework. Employing an extended six-factor linear model (incorporating Market, Size, Value, Profitability, Investment, and Momentum factors), we decompose the total variance of diversified tactical equity allocations to isolate the true drivers of return behavior.

Our findings indicate that the market factor systematically dominates the total variance of multi-tilted equity portfolios, absorbing the overwhelming majority of systematic return dynamics. When individual sector or thematic bets are analyzed in isolation, they exhibit substantial specific variance; however, once aggregated into a multi-asset allocation, these idiosyncratic components largely cancel out due to structural factor overlap. 

The remaining portfolio return profile is primarily explained by broad systematic market risk, alongside minor factor exposures, leaving an statistically insignificant residual for pure active skill. Consequently, investors who build complex, highly-fragmented portfolios face a fundamental structural trade-off: isolated bets introduce uncompensated idiosyncratic noise, whereas diversified bets rapidly converge toward a costly proxy of broad systematic market exposure. We discuss the implications of these empirical dynamics for portfolio design, fee efficiency, and asset allocation strategy.

title: The unintended distributional consequences of public data openness: Evidence from regional debt financing dispersion in China
affiliations: South-Central Minzu University, South-Central Minzu University and Xiamen University - Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE)

detail.title: The unintended distributional consequences of public data openness: Evidence from regional debt financing dispersion in China
detail.abstract: Abstract: This study examines the distributional consequences of public data openness for regional debt financing. Exploiting the staggered rollout of municipal public data platforms across Chinese cities from 2009 to 2023, we find that public data openness significantly increases within-city debt financing dispersion. The financing gains accrue disproportionately to state-owned enterprises, more digitalized firms, and firms with stronger government–business connections. This effect is amplified by local artificial intelligence development but mitigated by a better information environment, stronger financial regulation, and higher local governance efficiency. These findings demonstrate that public data openness can widen financing disparities despite reducing information frictions, highlighting the importance of institutional safeguards in promoting more inclusive use of public data and data-driven technologies.

title: A Two-Stage Array Optimization Scheme for UAV with DNN-Assisted Improved Genetic Algorithm and fmincon Optimizer
affiliations: Xidian University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, North University of China, Xidian University and National University of Singapore (NUS)

detail.title: A Two-Stage Array Optimization Scheme for UAV with DNN-Assisted Improved Genetic Algorithm and fmincon Optimizer
detail.abstract: Non-uniform arrays (NUAs), which enjoy low sidelobe levels (SLL) and lightweight hardware structure, overcome the performance limitations of uniform arrays (UAs), especially for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). However, existing array optimization methods suffer from high computational complexity and susceptibility to local optima. To cope with these issues, we propose a two-stage array optimization scheme with DNN-assisted improved Genetic Algorithm (GA) and fmincon optimizer. First, a population global optimization algorithm with DNN-assisted improved genetic algorithm is proposed, which replaces the computationally expensive exact physical fitness function, enhances gene recombination, mitigates population homogenization, and thus achieves both high efficiency and high accuracy. After the dataset is established, the trained DNN maps low-dimensional parameters to high-dimensional feature spaces, decomposes complex electromagnetic coupling layer by layer, and realizes high-precision predictions, avoiding redundant radiation calculations. Moreover, to eliminate residual error between surrogate model predictions and true SLL, an individual precision optimization is proposed, which combines the exact physics fitness function with the fmincon optimizer to remove prediction biases. Finally, extensive simulations verify the feasibility and superiority of our scheme for non-uniform linear arrays (NULA) and non-uniform circular arrays (NUCA). Therefore, this work provides an efficient, hardware-simplified tool for rapid UAV antenna design.

title: Efficiency and Cost-Benefit of Arbovirus Interventions: A Multi-Criteria Approach to Support Public Decision-Making
affiliations: UFF - Universidade Federal Fluminense, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Universidade Federal Fluminense, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Efficiency and Cost-Benefit of Arbovirus Interventions: A Multi-Criteria Approach to Support Public Decision-Making
detail.abstract: This study employs multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA). The analysis incorporates economic, epidemiological, and operational data, including insights from Brazil’s 2024 dengue epidemic and mass vaccination campaigns in Dourados-MS. Innovative tools like the WebDengue® system enhance real-time surveillance and decision-making. Using Gaussian AHP and AHP-4AG methods to evaluate arbovirus control strategies in Brazil, comparing vaccination programs and vector control by endemic agents. The historically relevant Oswaldo Cruz System underpins Brazil’s public health surveillance and vector control efforts, emphasising manual and technological integration for effective disease management. The study indicates that vector control using endemic agents surpasses vaccination alone in coverage, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness, especially for dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever. Vaccines such as QDenga® and Dengvaxia® reduce symptoms and lower hospitalisation rates but face limitations in coverage and cost, restricting their standalone impact. The study advocates integrated investment in vaccination and vector control, supporting sustainable public health policies to mitigate the arbovirus burden nationally.
